behaviour: A ledger warning raised through raise_warning or built through new_alert needs only the revision and the time of the sync that raises it, not the whole op context: an open alert of the same text, or of the same sync writer and item, is left alone or has its last refusal time moved; a closed alert whose text is already known before the first alert of its sync is not raised again; every other case appends one new alert row carrying that revision and time and marks the context dirty. warning_raised and alert_row do this directly from a plain revision and time, with no context object at all, so a caller that only has those two values, such as PostgresLedgerRepository.admit, never has to build a stand-in for one.
seam: scripts.swarm_ledger.ledger_alerts.warning_raised and scripts.swarm_ledger.ledger_alerts.alert_row, called by raise_warning, new_alert and scripts.swarm_ledger.repository.postgres.PostgresLedgerRepository.admit
